name: divine word
lore:
# On the Utterance of the Divine Word

To speak the *Divine Word* is to briefly borrow the tongue of the Architect. When cast, the Weave does not merely bend; it snaps into a state of crystalline rigidity, vibrating with a frequency that resonates in the very marrow of one’s soul. To the observer, the caster does not merely speak; they erupt. A halo of prismatic resonance shatters the air, and the spoken syllable manifests as a visible shockwave of golden geometry, rewriting local reality to exclude the profane.

Legend attributes its discovery to Saint Valerius during the Siege of the Iron Gate. Facing a legion of the abyss, Valerius found his prayers exhausted. In the terrifying silence, he claimed to hear the "Primordial Hum" of creation itself. He mimicked a single note of that celestial song, and the demonic host did not merely die—they were unmade, their essences scattered back to the void by the sheer weight of absolute law.

Beware, traveler: such power taxes the mortal frame. One cannot speak the language of stars without scorching the throat and trembling for days thereafter.
